Attach your own ggplot beside the heatmap

Source: R/panel.R
calor_panel.Rd

Puts any ggplot on one side of the heatmap and lines it up cell by cell. Map the row names (for "left" and "right") to y, or the column names (for "top" and "bottom") to x; ggcalor places each name at its row or column, following the clustering, ordering and splits. Everything else (geoms, the value axis, scales, theme, legend) stays as you wrote it.

Usage

calor_panel(plot, side = c("right", "left", "top", "bottom"), size = 25)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with the row or column names mapped to y or x.

side

"right", "left", "top" or "bottom".

size

Panel thickness in millimetres (width for left and right, height for top and bottom).

Value

An object to add to a ggcalor() plot with +.

Details

Names in the plot's data that are not in the heatmap are dropped with ggplot2's usual warning. The along axis gets no labels or title of its own: the heatmap's names are drawn once, on the outermost track.

Examples

m <- scale(as.matrix(mtcars[1:12, 1:6]))
cars <- data.frame(car = rownames(m), mpg = mtcars$mpg[1:12])
bar <- ggplot2::ggplot(cars, ggplot2::aes(mpg, car)) + ggplot2::geom_col()
ggcalor(m) + calor_dendro(rows = TRUE) + calor_panel(bar, side = "right")
